clue.text: It's sweet of fellow to go in to cost

indicators.note: the fellow is told to go in, so his letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a fee is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether a sweet treat is worth what a fellow pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' says the fellow's letter goes inside the 'to' + 'cost' pair, splitting them; 'of' is a link word, so 'It's sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, a classic example of a sweet.

clue.text: Time foreign currency dealers started to get worried

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

indicators.note: the dealers have only just started, so take the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: A trader recalls the moment the currency desk began to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' takes the first letter of 'dealers', D, after T and ROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubled and worried are synonyms describing an anxious state of mind.

clue.text: Tufts of hair on Arab folks etc are rearranged

indicators.note: the words folks and etc are said to be put in a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Something about Arab people and their belongings being reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a people but is the horse breed; FOLKS + ETC shuffled by 'are rearranged' give the tufts above a horse's hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetlocks are the tufts of hair growing at the back of a horse's leg above the hoof, and an Arab is a breed of horse.

clue.text: Titles carry arms — dole

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Titles carry arms — dole' with no count: ARMS + DOLE is anagram fodder for EARLDOMS but the anagram indicator after 'dole' is cut off and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Force outside broadcast to return to sovereign

indicators.note: the force verb sits outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: to impel is to force or drive

indicators.note: the broadcast is sent back, so its letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Coercion beyond the airwaves restores power to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns the broadcast word back to front, and 'outside' wraps the force verb round it; the second 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an emperor or empire, hence sovereign in the sense of supreme ruling.

clue.text: Run into state trooper

indicators.note: the run is put into the state, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: Maine is a US state
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A soldier dashes across a state border.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier serving with a navy, and a trooper is a soldier.

clue.text: Turns out I've gone over to the courts

indicators.note: I've is said to have gone over, flipped end to end, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the contraction's letters as written, apostrophe dropped
CT is the abbreviation for court, so CTS for courts

explanation.surface: Someone explains they've handed a matter over to the legal system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' turns 'I've' back to front; 'Turns out' reads as 'it happens' in the surface, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict tenants is to turn them out of their home.

clue.text: Where I'm taking lots of time on the pictures

parts.note: the contraction's letters as written, apostrophe dropped
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Someone takes forever at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' and 'taking' are link words joining I'M and AGES; 'the pictures' suggests the cinema, but the definition is just pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or likenesses.

clue.text: Superficial gloss on a five year period

explanation.surface: A sheen applied to a stretch of five years.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rarer one, a variant of lustrum, the Roman five-year period.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a surface shine or sheen; it is also an old word for a lustrum, a span of five years.

clue.text: Court reversal in your agonised protest

indicators.note: the turned court piece is placed in the rearranged word
your is tortured into a new arrangement of letters
the court abbreviation undergoes reversal, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A legal ruling overturned leaves someone crying out in anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' turns the court abbreviation round; 'agonised' scrambles 'your' to OURY, and 'in' puts the turned pair inside it after OU.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest.

clue.text: America strains to produce skilled workers

indicators.note: the letters are worked over to produce a new word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: The USA pushes hard to create a skilled workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus STRAINS is rearranged by 'to produce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisans are craftspeople, workers trained in a manual skill.

clue.text: Lionheart originally abandoned his minstrel — was that fair?

indicators.note: the letter is abandoned, dropped from the minstrel's name

parts.note: Blondel was the legendary minstrel of Richard the Lionheart

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the king's epithet

explanation.surface: Was King Richard right to desert his faithful minstrel?
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the minstrel Blondel found the captive Richard I; 'abandoned' drops L, the first letter of 'Lionheart', from BLONDEL. 'fair' looks like justice but means fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A blonde person has fair hair, so fair is a synonym for light-haired.

clue.text: Tinker around with a winter wardrobe

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles about with their cold-weather clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: TINKER + W + A are rearranged by 'around'; 'Tinker' looks like a verb on the wardrobe but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted jumpers and cardigans are typical clothing for the cold months.

clue.text: Murderers risk trouble to bring measure up inside

indicators.note: the measure is placed inside the other letters
risk is troubled, stirred into a new arrangement
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Killers take a chance by smuggling in a measuring tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' scrambles 'risk' (to KIRS); 'up' turns the old measure upwards, as this is a down clue; 'inside' splits KI from RS round it. 'to bring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers and murderers are synonyms for those who take life.

clue.text: Story of place in France lacking a university

indicators.note: the word is lacking a letter, which is removed

parts.note: lieu is French for place
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A tale about a French town without a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place in France' suggests a town, but it is the French word for place, LIEU; 'lacking' removes U.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a false story, a fib.

clue.text: Little Michael's involved with old northerner

indicators.note: the letters become involved, tangled into a new order

parts.note: Mike is a short form of Michael, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Young Mike gets mixed up with someone from the far north long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles the short Michael's name with its possessive S, and the old abbreviation follows; the answer is now a dated term for Arctic peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: The term once used for Arctic peoples such as the Inuit, so a dweller of the far north.

clue.text: Even characters in Orwell disappear like a wise old bird

indicators.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the author's name are the even ones
the even letters vanish, so only the odd letters remain

explanation.surface: Letters go missing from Orwell's writing, wisely.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R, E and L from ORWELL leaves the odd letters; 'like' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are traditionally pictured as wise, and a wise old bird is a sage person.

clue.text: I object to new pieces on board

parts.note: me is the object form of the pronoun I

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest, but means I in its object case, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess and draughts pieces are often called men.

clue.text: Increased in size and volume

parts.note: a description of something puffed up, grown bigger and fuller than before

explanation.surface: A plain statement that something grew bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloated has grown larger in both size and bulk.

clue.text: Birth of main force accepting it in both senses

indicators.note: the fleet accepts the other letters inside itself
the word it sits in the fleet once in each direction

parts.note: the navy is the force at sea, the main being the ocean

indicators.note: both senses means both directions, so one copy of it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A navy welcomes a newcomer in two ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The one 'it' serves twice: 'both senses' makes one copy run backwards (TI) and 'accepting' with 'in' puts both inside the fleet, either side of its V. 'main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nativity is the birth of Christ, and nativity means birth generally.

clue.text: Spreading out from a group who want to do a Paris trip

indicators.note: the words trip up and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A party of people planning an outing to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like the journey but rearranges DO A PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people away from their homeland.

clue.text: They can't make an issue at Cheltenham, for example

definitions.text: They can't make an issue at Cheltenham, for example

parts.words: They can't make an issue at Cheltenham, for example
parts.note: issue means offspring; castrated racehorses running at Cheltenham cannot sire foals

explanation.surface: Some people are unable to raise a complaint at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a dispute but means offspring; Cheltenham is an English racecourse famous for jump racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated male horses cannot father foals, and many race at Cheltenham.

clue.text: Second attempt to get inside unsophisticated local

indicators.note: the letter is told to get inside the other word

parts.note: naive means unsophisticated or innocent

indicators.note: Second picks out the second letter of the word attempt

explanation.surface: Trying again to win over a simple resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second attempt' looks like a retry, but it is the second letter of 'attempt', T, placed inside NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place, a local inhabitant.

clue.text: Shoots the young people

explanation.surface: Someone opens fire on the youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprigs are small shoots or twigs; sprig is also a dated word for a youngster.

clue.text: A peal of bells could upset the French

parts.note: to trip someone is to upset them, make them fall
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Church bell ringing might annoy the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' is a link word; in change ringing triples are peals on seven bells.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell ringing, triples is a method rung on seven bells, giving a type of peal.

clue.text: It's wrong to take action against the paper

indicators.note: the letters of it's are wrongly ordered

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against

explanation.surface: Someone thinks suing a newspaper is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns ITS into TIS, then SUE; 'the paper' suggests a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin soft paper.

clue.text: Make a mistake by leaving the fruit

indicators.note: the letters of by are leaving, taken out of the fruit

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: Walking away from the fruit was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes B and Y (scattered, in order) from BERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to blunder or go wrong.

clue.text: Another ten engineers start to eat the dish

indicators.note: another arrangement of ten is wanted, signalling an anagram

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the start of eat, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Ten more engineers begin to tuck into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' rearranges TEN into ENT; RE; 'start to' takes E from 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a course of a meal, a dish.

clue.text: Sprint round and round staggered sections

indicators.note: a staggered runner lurches about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a second O for the second round

explanation.surface: A runner, lapping the track, staggers.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRINT + O + O are rearranged by 'staggered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Portions are parts or shares of a whole.

clue.text: Showed disapproval of man's second edition

parts.note: his is the possessive belonging to a man

explanation.surface: Someone frowned on a man's revised book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences hiss to express displeasure.

clue.text: They place burdens to impress doctors — there's nothing in it

indicators.note: nothing is in it, inside the rearranged letters
to doctor is to tamper, so impress is altered into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Burdensome people try to win over medics, but it's empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like a noun but rearranges IMPRESS; 'in' puts O inside: IMP-O-SERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who impose are those who lay burdens or demands on others.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge being depressed when one's inside

indicators.note: one's is placed inside the other word

parts.note: down means depressed
one is I, so one's (one is) is I + S

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low won't recognise a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'one's' is I + S, put inside DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject or refuse to recognise them.

clue.text: Pinned down in gardens among variety of reeds

indicators.note: the gardens are among the other letters
a variety of reeds means its letters in a different arrangement

parts.note: Kew Gardens is the botanic garden in London

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a garden bed among the reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' turns REEDS into SERED; 'among' puts KEW in: S-KEW-ERED. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered means pierced and held fast, like something pinned.

clue.text: Operate on the ring road

explanation.surface: Surgery on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: A bypass is heart surgery that reroutes blood; it is also a road round a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a surgical rerouting round a blockage; a bypass is also a road skirting a town centre.
